full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury, J: This Rule is directed against an order of the executing court refusing to stay further proceedings for execution of a decree for eviction of a monthly tenant from certain shop premises. The prayer for stay was made by the petitioner on the ground that the decree under execution had been challenged in a suit before the senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet, Regard being had to the facts of the case the executing court took a view that it was no longer open to the petitioner to ask for stay of the execution proceedings. In order to determine the correctness of the view it will be necessary to make a brief statement of facts. 

 2. One Taib Ali, who happens to be the father of the petitioner, was a monthly tenant in the said shop premises under the opposite party. In 1973 the opposite party as plaintiff brought a suit being Title Suit No. 140 of 1973 in the court of the Munsif, Sadar, Sylhet for eviction of the monthly tenant from the premises. Taib Ali contested the suit, but it was decreed by the trial Court. The decree was, however, set aside in appeal. On further appeal to the High Court Division the appellate decree was set aside and the Judgment and the decree of the trial Court was restored. Taib Ali then prayed for special leave to appeal to the Appellate Division which was refused on 28.5.89. 

 3. In the meantime the decree holder opposite party put the decree into execution in Title Execution No. 2 of 1989 in the court of Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet. The present petitioner filed an application before the executing court on 10.6.89 praying for stay of further proceeding of the Execution Case till the hearing or Title Suit No. 174 of 1989 filed by him in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet on or about 4.6.89. It was claimed in suit that he purchased the disputed property on 30.5.89 from some of its owners. and a decree in Title Suit No. 140 of 1973 was not binding on him. The prayer for stay was opposed by the decree holder on the plea that the petitioner had been set up by the Judgment-debtor, only to deprive the decree holder of the fruits of his decree. The executing court after a hearing rejected the prayer of the petitioner on 28.8.89. The unsuccessful petitioner then preferred a revisional application before a vacation Bench of the High Court Division at Sylhet and obtained an order dated 11.10.89 in Civil Order No. 851 of 1959, staying further proceeding of the execution case till the hearing of the substantive revisional application after the re-opening. The decree holder, however, made a prayer for vacating the said stay order and a Single Bench of this Court, by an order dated 21.3.90, allowed the prayer on the following view: 

 "It is submitted by Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate on behalf of the opposite party that although the opposite party got the decree for eviction of the tenant as far back in 1976 and the decree for eviction was affirmed by this court, The decree holder opposite party has been deprived of the fruits of the litigation at the instance of the 3rd party being the son of the judgment-debtor. 

 The petitioner thereafter made no effort to get the revisional application heard. He filed a fresh petition before the executing court and renewed his prayer for stay of the execution proceeding. By the impugned order dated 15.5.90 the executing court rejected the said application on the view that it was no longer open to the petitioner to maintain a fresh application for stay on the self-same facts. In my opinion the order suffers from no error of law for the following reasons: Firstly, the petitioner being a third party to the decree has no locus standito maintain an application for stay of the execution proceeding, and secondly, the facts of the case do not also warrant an exercise of the discretionary power of the Court to make an order of stay.
